boot.evidence: Guest boots in every B3 phase: the initial up, the post-SIGKILL restart, and the final teardown all report a live kernel (7.2.0-rc4-g169b17ff3f66-dirty, seccomp, ncpus=4) and the guest reaches WEB_UP_MARKER with a running container. The kernel release is taken from the guest, not from the boot arguments.

b3_restart_and_exposure_reapply.evidence: B3 passes end to end: instance ready, a real container serving 8123 inside the guest (WEB_UP_MARKER), an exposure 18131->8123 that a host curl reaches (banner gvproxy-bess-ok), a SIGKILL of the daemon after which the forwarder dies with it, a restart through the plain supervisor adapter with a new daemon pid (7573 -> 10336), and after that restart the SAME host curl reaches the container again -- the recorded exposure was re-applied, not re-created by hand. Teardown left 0 processes.

c_daemon_ssh_port_parity_gap.evidence: Found by B3: the C daemon never honoured UML4TERMUXD_GVPROXY_SSH_PORT, so gvproxy was always started with its default 127.0.0.1:2222 SSH forwarder and a second instance (or a restart next to a leftover) died with 'bind: address already in use'. The Rust daemon has honoured it since the multi-instance round -- a real behaviour divergence. Fixed in src/uml4termuxd.c (argv now carries -ssh-port=<n> when the env var is set); the gvproxy command line in the B3 log shows ssh-port=12600.

orphan_children_on_sigkill.evidence: Found by B3: SIGKILLing the daemon left its gvproxy alive, holding the host ports, so the restarted instance could not bind them and a later expose came back as gvproxy HTTP 500 ('bind: address already in use' in gvproxy's own log). Fixed with prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM) in both child branches (gvproxy and the guest kernel), so the kernel reaps them when the daemon dies; the successful B3 run ends with 0 leftover processes.

unix_socket_path_truncation.evidence: Found while a soak run put its runtime dir inside a deep repo path: three strncpy(addr.sun_path, ...) sites silently TRUNCATED a path longer than 107 bytes, so the daemon would bind or connect to a different path than the one it printed -- gvproxy then died with 'bind: invalid argument' while the daemon reported no problem. Now sockpath_too_long() refuses loudly, and the launcher checks the runtime dir up front (runtime 92 bytes + 17 = 109 >= 107 -> exit 64 with the numbers and a suggested fix).

notes: Direction B, item B3 only; B1 (2 h soak) and B2 (two parallel guests) run separately and get their own record. The B3 harness answers 'is the port listening?' with a real HTTP request because /proc/net/tcp is denied to the Termux app, and it keeps the guest alive with the repo's docker-init.sh (GUEST_LIFETIME=0) because a guest that powers off makes the daemon exit normally.
known_limits_observed: the exposure test depends on a container image being available in the guest (pull through gvproxy NAT)
the first B3 attempt reported a false failure because a stray forwarder from an earlier interrupted run still held the port; the harness now probes the port and moves to the next one
